Possession
poz-zesh'un
n. (a holding, that which is owned; rendering Hebrew achuzzah, Greek peripoiesis)
From the Latin possessio, from possideo, to have and hold. Hebrew achuzzah is from achaz, to grasp or seize, and denotes a holding granted by another — in the Law, land held from the LORD, who declares that the land is his and Israel are strangers and sojourners with him.

Biblical Definition

Possession in Scripture is almost always a granted holding, not an absolute ownership, and the distinction runs through the whole covenant. To Abraham God says he will give the land of his sojourning “for an everlasting possession” (Genesis 17:8) — a gift with a giver, held on terms. Israel's tenure in Canaan is therefore conditional in its enjoyment though unbreakable in its promise, and the jubilee laws exist to keep any family from being permanently dispossessed, since the land could not finally be sold, only leased until the year of release. The Psalter extends the grant to the Son: “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession” (Psalm 2:8). Then the New Testament performs its characteristic reversal. Believers are not merely those who receive a possession; they are one. The Spirit is “the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession” (Ephesians 1:14) — the church is God's own holding, bought with blood, and the Spirit is the down payment guaranteeing that the buyer will take delivery. Moses had said as much of Israel long before: “For the LORD'S portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance” (Deuteronomy 32:9).

Webster 1828 Definition

A holding granted by another. Israel's land was held from the LORD, never owned absolutely; and in the New Testament believers are themselves God's purchased possession, with the Spirit as the earnest.

expand to see more

POSSESSION, n. [L. possessio.] The having, holding or detention of property in one's power or command; actual seizin or occupancy.

2. The thing possessed; land, estate, or goods owned; as, the possessions of a family.

3. The state of being under the dominion of another power; as, possession by an evil spirit.

4. In Scripture, an inheritance granted by God and held from him; as, an everlasting possession, Gen. 17.

5. Of the church, the purchased possession, redeemed unto God, Eph. 1.

Key Scripture

Genesis 17:8 — "And I will give unto thee, and to thy seed after thee, the land wherein thou art a stranger, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession; and I will be their God."

Psalm 2:8 — "Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession."

Ephesians 1:14 — "Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory."

Deuteronomy 32:9 — "For the LORD'S portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance."

Modern Corruption

Ownership is now conceived as absolute — what is mine is mine to use, keep, or destroy. Scripture grants real property rights and grounds them in a prior divine ownership that makes every holding a stewardship.

expand to see more

Two errors flank this word and Scripture refuses both. The collectivist error denies private property outright, which the eighth commandment forbids: thou shalt not steal presupposes that something belonged to someone. The absolutist error says property is held without account, which the jubilee legislation flatly contradicts — the land could not be permanently alienated, because the LORD says the land is his. Between them stands stewardship: real ownership, really answerable.

The deeper recovery is the direction of the word in the New Testament. Ephesians 1:14 makes the believer the property rather than the proprietor, and 1 Corinthians states the ground: ye are not your own, for ye are bought with a price. That single fact reorders the questions men ask about their bodies, their time, their money, and their children. A man who understands himself as a purchased possession will still hold things, and hold them gladly, but he will hold them as a tenant whose Landlord is coming to take delivery.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew achuzzah is a holding, from achaz, to grasp; nachalah is the inheritance-portion allotted by lot. Greek peripoiesis is a possession or acquisition, and kleronomia the inheritance.

expand to see more

Hebrew achuzzah (H272) — a possession, a holding; the term for tribal land tenure in Canaan.

Hebrew achaz (H270) — to seize, to grasp, to hold fast; the verbal root.

Hebrew nachalah (H5159) — inheritance, heritage; the LORD's portion is his people.

Greek peripoiesis (G4047) — a purchased possession, an acquiring; used of the church in Ephesians 1:14.

Greek arrhabon (G728) — earnest, pledge, down payment; the Spirit as guarantee of the rest.

Usage

"Of the land granted to Abraham on terms: for an everlasting possession (Genesis 17:8)."

"Of the nations given to the Son: the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession (Psalm 2:8)."

"Of the church as God's own holding: the redemption of the purchased possession (Ephesians 1:14)."
